assumptions.text: Small software teams spend too much time writing release notes and changelogs.
developers and product managers at small SaaS companies have this problem.
This solves it: A web app that drafts customer-facing release notes from a small software team's merged pull requests, for a person to edit and publish.
These customers can be reached in: English-speaking small SaaS companies, online.
The founder can build and test it with: Python and web development, technical writing; 10 hours a week; 300 EUR.
Enough of these customers would pay for it.

new_hypotheses.text: Small software teams might prefer manual release note creation over automated tools due to customization needs

risks.text: The problem might not be widespread enough to justify automation
Automated release notes might not be accurate without significant customization

experiments.name: Test manual vs automated time
experiments.method: Ask 5 small software teams to write release notes manually and via the web app
experiments.weaken_if: Manual takes less time or automated is less accurate

experiments.name: Test problem severity
experiments.method: Survey 20 small software teams about time spent on release notes
experiments.support_if: More than 50% spend over 1 hour per release
experiments.weaken_if: Less than 20% spend over 1 hour per release
